tools.name: whoami
tools.title: Show my account
tools.description: Who this connection edits as: the account email, its plan, its credits (as the app shows them), what this server may spend, and how many check renders are left today. Every tool is free except generate_image, which takes 50 credits per image from this account, the transcription of import_media (10 credits per started 2 minutes of media) and export_video (10 credits per started minute of the edited video). availableHere says whether this server reaches the stock libraries (search_stock) and the image model (generate_image); when it cannot reach the image model (a local server never can), generate_image is refused before any charge. The renders that check your work (measure_scene, look_at_montage, look_at_source, the measure of check_edit, check_audio) are free within a daily allowance per account, back at midnight UTC.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: The account's projects (its own, those shared with it and its teams'), most recently CREATED first, searched and paged over ALL of them: id, name, createdAt, updatedAt, sourceDurationSec (the length of the source video, null when unknown), format, whether it has a transcript and a video, your role, and copiedFrom (the original's id and name) for a copy. Filter by name with query (part of the name, any case). total is how many match; when nextCursor is not null, pass it back as cursor for the next page. The edited length of a project is in get_project_state (montageDurationSec).

limit.description: How many per page (default 20, at most 50).

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page.

tools.name: get_project_state
tools.title: Get project state
tools.description: Open a project and read its state: format, montage length, transcript size and how much is cut, every B-roll and every zoom with its id and its moment (word keys fromKey/toKey, which the gestures take, and montage seconds, which look_at_montage takes), captions, music, silences, and editRevision (give it back as expectedRevision when you write). Read it first, and again after a conflict.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

tools.name: clone_project
tools.title: Clone project
tools.description: Copy a project you own into a new project of the same account, and return the new id and name. Two copies, the same as the two choices of the app's Duplicate action. By default (fresh: true) it is "Duplicate from scratch": the copy starts as right after the transcription: the video, its proxy, what the app measured of it (face, camera card, what the source shows) and the transcript; no cut, no moved passage, no scene or other B-roll, no zoom, no subtitle, no music, no sound effect, silences as recorded. This is the copy for a full edit from scratch. fresh: false is "Duplicate": the whole edit comes along too (cuts, moved passages, B-rolls with their sound effects, zooms, subtitles, music), only when the creator asks to continue an existing edit on a copy. Give the copy a clear name (for example "<video name> - <what this edit is>"): the creator finds it by that name. Edit the copy, not the original, unless the creator asked otherwise. Both copies follow the limits of the account, exactly like creating a project in the app: the plan's number of projects, the storage space, only the project's owner can copy it, and a paused or suspended account cannot. A refused copy says why, and nothing is created.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

name.description: The copy's name, clear for the creator, kept as given (default: the app's numbered name, « <name> (copie 2) », « (copie 3) »… or « (copy 2) » in English).

fresh.description: true (default): "Duplicate from scratch", the copy starts as right after the transcription (the video and its transcript), nothing of the edit comes along. false: "Duplicate", the whole edit comes along.

tools.name: start_over
tools.title: Start the edit over
tools.description: Put a project back as right after the transcription: the video, its proxy, what the app measured of it (face, camera card, what the source shows) and the transcript; no cut, no moved passage, no scene or other B-roll, no zoom, no subtitle, no music, no sound effect, silences as recorded, by the same code as the app's "Start over" box: every cut word restored, moved passages back in place, corrected words and hand-set word timings undone, every B-roll (with its sound effects) and every zoom removed, subtitles, background music and voice settings cleared. The video and the transcript stay. Destructive: it needs confirm: true, and a checkpoint is saved first so the creator can restore the edit. To keep the original untouched, prefer clone_project, which makes a fresh copy by default.

projectId.description: The project id (from list_projects or clone_project).

expectedRevision.description: The editRevision you last read; a different one means the project changed: nothing is applied.

tools.description: Add or remove one of the creator's favourites, like the star in the Studio: `kind` (music, sfx, element, caption-style) and `id` (a track id from list_music, a sound id from list_sfx, an element id from list_favorites such as text:title or shape:arrow, a style id from get_captions), `favorite` true to add, false to remove. Only when the creator asks. At most 60 per kind. Free.

tools.name: import_media
tools.title: Import media
tools.description:
Create a new project from a video or audio file, the way the app's import does it, and return at once job_id, project_id and project_url. One source:
- add_media (direct upload): {"<file name>": {"content_type": "video/mp4", "file_size": <bytes>}}. The result gives upload_urls[<file name>] = {upload_url, asset_id, headers}: PUT the raw bytes of the file to upload_url with the header Content-Type: application/octet-stream (no form, no encoding); the size must equal file_size, and the address works once. If the PUT fails, call report_upload_status with status failed.
- add_media with {"<name>": {"url": "https://..."}}, or url: a direct link to a media file (not a page that plays one).
- path: an absolute path to a file, or to a folder (with file naming the one to take), ONLY on the local server and ONLY inside a folder the creator allowed (a root of the MCP client, or --allow-dir when the local server is launched); the original is copied, never moved.
- drop: true, when you cannot send the file yourself (a web chat with no terminal): the result gives drop_page_url, a Brollss page where the creator drops the file. Give that link to the creator, then wait_for_job. add_media also returns drop_page_url, for the same case.
Then call wait_for_job with job_id: the server transcribes the voice (on its own machine or its own transcription worker, never a third party) and puts the transcript, the video, an editing proxy and a poster in the project. Then get_project_state on project_id and edit. Paid: the transcription costs 10 credits per started 2 minutes of media (a 9-minute video costs 50 credits), the same price as an import in the app, taken from this account when the file has arrived and before the transcription starts, and given back if it fails. Without enough credits the import stops with the reason. The plan's limits apply exactly as in the app: number of projects, file size. Never import again because a wait timed out: call wait_for_job again.

tools.name: get_job
tools.title: Check a job
tools.description: Where an import or an export stands, now, without waiting. An import: phase (uploading, copying, transcribing, delivering, ready, failed), progress {label, percent}, the step, the last log lines, the error in plain words when it failed, and the project once ready. An export (kind: export): phase (starting while its credits are taken, waiting_for_browser, preparing_scenes, browser_unsupported, assembling, ready, failed, cancelled), the scenes sent, export_page_url while the page is needed, download_url once ready, and the credits charged or given back. wait_for_job waits.

job_id.description: The job_id import_media or export_video returned.

tools.name: wait_for_job
tools.title: Wait for a job
tools.description: Wait for an import or an export, up to wait_seconds (local server: default 600, at most 1800; hosted: default 120, at most 300), and return its state as get_job does. done: true when it is ready (an import: edit project_id; an export: download_url serves the MP4 for one hour, and a new call gives a fresh one) or failed or cancelled (the error says why, and whether the credits were given back). An export whose scenes render in a browser without display on this machine (headless: true, the local case) needs nothing from you: keep waiting. Otherwise, an export waiting for its page (phase waiting_for_browser) returns at once with export_page_url: open it yourself, then wait again. An export with a warning (its page is in a background tab, or no scene has moved for 5 minutes) returns at once too: do what the warning says, then wait again. Still running when the wait ends (timed_out: true): call wait_for_job again. Never import or export again because of a timeout: that would make a second project or a second charge.

job_id.description: The job_id import_media or export_video returned.

tools.name: report_upload_status
tools.title: Report upload status
tools.description: Say how a direct upload went: status failed (with error) when the PUT to upload_url did not succeed, so the import stops cleanly instead of waiting; status uploaded is optional (wait_for_job notices the file by itself). To retry a failed upload, call import_media again.

job_id.description: The job_id import_media or export_video returned.

media_id.description: The file's key in upload_urls (the name given in add_media).

tools.name: export_video
tools.title: Export video
tools.description: Export the edited video as an MP4 the creator can download. PAID: 10 credits per started minute of the edited video (a 4 min 10 s montage costs 50 credits), the price of the Export button in the Studio, taken from this account. Two calls. Without confirm: nothing is charged; the result gives the price, the length and the number of scenes; tell the creator the price. With confirm: true: the credits are taken BEFORE anything starts, then the result gives export_page_url, a Brollss page that renders the scenes in the browser that opens it (no sign-in needed) and sends them to our server, which puts the video together. When this server runs on the creator's machine (the local server, or the app reached at an address of this machine), confirm: true opens that page itself in a browser without display on this machine, which renders the scenes until they are sent: you have nothing to open (the result says headless: true). Otherwise, or if that browser cannot start (the result says so), open it yourself: Open export_page_url YOURSELF, right away: in a visible tab in the foreground, with the machine's command, which opens the creator's own browser in front (Windows: start "" "<url>"; macOS: open "<url>"; Linux: xdg-open "<url>"), or in your own browser tool only if it shows a real visible tab that stays in front; or in a headless browser that you drive yourself (a headless Chrome renders the page normally). Never in a hidden or minimized window, nor a browser pane kept out of sight: a browser stops rendering a tab nobody sees, and the export stalls. Do not ask the creator to click it; ask them to open it only if you have no way at all to open a browser. Then call wait_for_job with job_id until done; at the end it gives download_url. The page must stay open, visible and in front while it prepares the scenes. A page not opened within 15 minutes, or on which no scene moves for 15 minutes (closed, hidden in a background tab, or stuck), cancels the export and gives the credits back; a failed export gives them back too, once. wait_for_job says when the page is in a background tab or no scene has moved for 5 minutes, and what to do. The same export already made is given back at once, free. The plan's watermark and quality apply, as in the Studio.

confirm.description: true to take the credits and start the export. Without it, only the price is returned.

quality.description: Default standard. Capped by the project owner's plan, as in the Studio.

tools.description: The outline of the WHOLE video: blocks of about 30 to 60 s with their time range, word keys, sentence count and first words. Cheap. Use it to plan the video; then read a block with read_transcript.

tools.name: read_transcript
tools.title: Read transcript
tools.description: Read the transcript in order, with a cursor: up to maxSentences sentences from a time (m:ss or seconds) or a word key, each as [m:ss] (first key..last key) text. The result gives `next`, where to continue (pass it as `from`: a long video reads page after page, past maxSentences), and what you have read of the whole video so far. `words: true` adds, under each sentence, the key of every word, to cut or correct inside a sentence. A passage you already read is not sent again while the transcript is unchanged: write what matters in your notebook as you read. On this server every time is a time of the MONTAGE; pass withSource: true to add the source time.

tools.name: find_hesitations
tools.title: Find hesitations
tools.description: Deterministically detect hesitations, by kind: `filler` (euh, um…), `repeat` (an immediate repeat), `restart` (a multi-word restart), `false_start` (an abandoned start). Returns candidates with their word keys and context, and the PAUSES the viewer hears longer than pauseOverSec (default 1 s). Nothing is cut: cut what deserves it with strike_words (fromKey/toKey from the candidate's keys), after reading the sentence around it. set_silences shortens every long pause at once.

tools.name: strike_words
tools.title: Cut words
tools.description: Cut ONE named passage of words the user points at (a phrase, a sentence). `cutMode` carries the two transcript-panel variants: omit it (or "remove") to take the words out of the script, "gap" to keep their duration as a black/silent gap. `fromKey`/`toKey` are word keys (segment:word, e.g. 16:2) copied from the firstKey/lastKey of read_transcript or search_transcript; a unit id such as s18 is not a key. This is the tool for "cut the sentence where I talk about X". For a pass over the WHOLE video (bad takes, anything that adds nothing), a gesture this server does not offer — never this.

tools.name: move_passage
tools.title: Move a passage
tools.description: Move a passage of WHOLE sentences so it plays elsewhere; nothing is cut. The hook gesture: leave beforeKey out and the passage becomes the very first thing heard, then the video goes on in its order (the greeting and intro follow it). To OPEN the video on its strongest sentence (a question, a figure, a promise), the passage IS that strong sentence and beforeKey is left out; never move the greeting or the announcement away instead. `fromKey` is the first word of the first sentence, `toKey` the last word of the last sentence (the one with the full stop), copied from the transcript. The passage must last 3 to 15 s. `beforeKey` only to place it before another sentence: the first word of that sentence. A passage that starts or ends mid-sentence is refused with the reason. This server adds `scenes`: "follow" (default) or "stay" (the B-rolls anchored on the passage keep their place in the montage). A B-roll that follows and outlasts its passage can be shortened with set_duration, or redrawn with measure_scene then insert_scene and its brollId.

scenes.description: What happens to the B-rolls anchored on the moved words. "follow" (default): they move with their sentence; when one lasts longer than the passage, the result says so. "stay": each one keeps its moment in the montage and is re-anchored on the word said there after the move (it then plays over other words).

tools.name: set_silences
tools.title: Set silence handling

The project state says whether it is ON now. breathMs is the pause kept at each cut (default 300 ms, the Studio's "natural" breath); set it only when the person asks for tighter (150) or calmer (600) cuts. For a full edit the code sets the editor's breath (leadMs before speech, tailMs after, longer; minGapMs: only longer pauses are cut); change it only when asked.

tools.name: look_at_source
tools.title: Look at the source video
tools.description: SEE the raw SOURCE video at one moment: returns the picture itself (JPEG), with a 12x12 grid drawn on it (columns A-L left to right, rows 1-12 top to bottom) to help you read positions. Every zone or box you give back to the tools (add_zoom zone, a face box) is in FRACTIONS 0-1 of THIS source picture: x, y of the top-left corner, w, h of the size; one grid cell is 1/12. Also returns what the project already measured there, without a new look: the speaker's `face` box and where it comes from (an earlier look, the map of the source, the face track, or on a screen share the camera card), `sourceShows` (speaker facing the camera, screen share with a camera card, screen alone) and, on a screen share, `cameraCard`. get_scene_brief, measure_scene and insert_scene use the same face when you omit `face`. Null face: nothing measured there; read it on the picture. `at`: montage seconds, "m:ss" or a word key; source:true reads `at` as source seconds. Free; ffmpeg, under 2 s.

tools.name: look_at_montage
tools.title: Look at the edit
tools.description: SEE your EDIT at one moment of the montage: renders the FINAL picture as the viewer will see it (the cut video, its zoom, every B-roll and scene on top, the speaker's card, the captions) and returns it (JPEG, 1280 px wide by default, no grid so nothing hides the face; grid: true adds the 12x12 grid), with what the code measures: the layers on screen and whether each is drawn, the speaker's face box measured before (fractions of the frame), the share of the face under each visual, the active zoom, the caption shown, and problems found. Look after placing or changing something, and before saying an edit is finished. Read-only and free; one render at a time (looks asked together wait for each other), 5 to 60 s each, so look at the moments that matter.

at.description: Montage seconds, "m:ss", or a word key.

grid.description: Draw the 12x12 grid over the picture (default false: it covers the face).

tools.name: check_edit
tools.title: Check the edit
tools.description: Check the whole edit, by code, free, no model. Three parts. `timeline`: what gets in each other's way on the export's timeline, each with its montage seconds and a fix: two scenes on the same layer at once, a scene drawn over another, a zoom under a scene (a zoom enlarges the video, never the scene: "zoom-under-full-frame" when the render shows the scene fills the frame, so the zoom is not seen; under a transparent P9 scene, only "zoom-pushes-face-under-scene" when the zoomed face goes under the scene's elements and "zoom-shifts-scene-target" when the part of the picture the scene marks slides away), an HTML page shortened or lengthened by more than 10 % or 50 % (the export plays its whole animation faster or slower to fit its block; nothing is cut), captions drawn over a scene, a visual past the end. What the cuts left behind: "visual-outside-montage" (its words cut up to the end: not shown), "visual-on-cut-words" (moved to a cut seam), "zoom-zero-length", "caption-passage-cut", each with its removal. In a shared screen with a detached speaker's card (it stays still while the screen zooms beside it): "zoom-shows-speaker-twice" (a zoom under it still shows the camera card of the source, so the speaker appears twice). When the speaker's video moves during a scene: "video-motion-twice-in-a-row" (two visuals in a row move it), "scene-under-moving-video" (a page drawn without the motion its row carries: it paints under the video), "flat-scene-without-motion" (a P9 page drawn for a moving video whose row lost the motion: its background covers the speaker), "video-motion-past-block" (the motion ends after its block: at the cut the video is still away from its place and jumps back). `scenes`: every scene's pace in its block: an HTML page the export plays faster (shortened) or slower (lengthened), or a ready-made template laid out again for its block (its pace kept). `rubric`: the publish-ready rubric (hook, too many visuals, visuals on each other, captions, retakes left, mid-sentence joins, zooms, music), what fails and how to fix it. No number of visuals per minute is required: the visual density, the pace and the stretches without a visual come in the rubric's `notes`, for information. `notes`: what was seen but needs no fix: "long-stretch-without-visual" (every stretch of 30 s or more with no visual, with what the source shows there, where the speaker is, and `zones`: the calm bands of the picture, such as black bands around a shared screen or a plain wall, where a P9 scene can play, in fractions of the frame, and `ideas`: what the speaker explains there that may ask for a picture, such as a list, a number, steps or a comparison, to answer one by one in a full edit; leaving the speaker alone there is a valid choice), subtitles at the bottom while a P9 scene's elements stay above them; the rubric's `notes` also say which taste limits a gesture the creator asked for lifts (a zoom or subtitles passed with `reason`). Notes never count as points to fix. Run it after a batch of gestures and before saying an edit is finished; then look_at_montage at the moments it names. With measure (default true) it renders one frame per scene that something overlaps, to tell a full-frame scene from a smaller one: 5 to 60 s.

measure.description: Render the frames that tell whether a scene fills the frame (default true). false: timeline only, a few seconds.

tools.name: list_zooms
tools.title: List zooms
tools.description: The punch-in zooms already on the video: id, scale, motion and moment (fromKey/toKey, the word keys the gestures take, and montageStartSec/montageEndSec, the seconds look_at_montage takes). Call it before update_zoom or remove_zooms; a zoom id never comes from you.

tools.name: add_zoom
tools.title: Add zoom
tools.description: Add a punch-in zoom from startWordKey to endWordKey (or for durationSec). To show a part of the SCREEN the speaker talks about (a button, a menu, a line of code), pass `zone`: the rectangle you read on look_at_source, in fractions of the source picture; the code picks the scale and the framing that show the whole zone (the strongest allowed zoom is x1.6, so a small zone gets x1.6 centred on it, and a zone covering nearly the whole frame is refused with the reason). Without zone, give scale (1.05 to 1.6) and, only for a deliberate off-centre framing, focusX/focusY (crop-slack fractions); without them the app frames on the subject it detects. motion: snap (default), push (slow push-in), punch (hit and overshoot), keyframes (any curve or pan; not with zone). The result gives the frame actually set. When the creator asked for this zoom, pass `reason` (their request in one line): check_edit then reports the zoom spacing and count limits as a note, not a point to fix. A zoom enlarges the source video only, never a scene, title or image placed over it (the preview and the export do the same): under a full-frame scene it is not seen; under a transparent P9 scene the scene stays put while the face and the screen grow and slide behind it, so a mark drawn on a button no longer sits on it. check_edit names only these conflicts. Under the speaker's detached card (a shared screen where the speaker's card stays still while the screen zooms beside it), the zoom must never show the camera card of the source: the result moves the framing until that card leaves the frame (same scale), or refuses the zoom when no framing at that scale does; it is never widened to keep the card whole there, since the speaker would then appear twice.

tools.description:
Turn the project's subtitle track on or off. When on, every spoken word of the montage is captioned (2 lines max, cut words skipped, the word being spoken highlighted) and burned into the export. This is the tool for subtitles on the WHOLE video, when the user asks for that ("captions on the whole video", "sous-titres sur toute la vidéo"). One call covers the whole video: no word keys. A full edit does not turn it on unless asked: it places subtitles on a few key passages with add_caption. `preset`: bold (default, big uppercase, highlighted word), karaoke (coloured active word), clean (plain white), minimal (small, on a dark box). `position` bottom|middle|top. The style is set here too, when the user asks: `color` is the text colour (#rrggbb, or yellow, white, red, green, blue, orange, pink, purple, cyan, black; French names too), `highlightColor` the colour of the word being spoken (never the text colour: it would not show, so the code switches it to white, or yellow on white text), `sizePct` the size in % of the frame's short side (clean 5, bold 6.5; "bigger" is 8 to 10, max 12). A preset resets the style, so send the colour and size in the same call as the preset. `highlight` and `maxWordsPerLine` only when the user asks. enabled:false removes them. `style` puts a whole look from the subtitle catalogue at once (font, colours, spoken word, box, animation), by name; the position, a size the creator set and the passages stay. When the creator chose the style (on the track, or as their default), keep it: no style, preset or colours unless they ask for a new look. When they have not, a full edit picks the style that suits the video.

Through this server: get_captions lists the catalogue styles (`catalogue`: id, French and English names, family) for `style`. The answer reads back the track as written: each passage with its keys, montage start and end in seconds and its words, and the style it wears. When the creator chose the subtitle style (styleBy creator, or a default style on the account), style, preset and colours are left out unless you pass lookAsked: true because the creator asked to change their look.

tools.name: set_music
tools.title: Set music
tools.description: Set the background music from the library (the track id comes from list_music, or `find` picks the best match for tags: style, mood, use, energy, bpmMin, bpmMax, text) over the whole video, or clear it with trackId: null. Without `volume`, the level starts where the app's mixer starts: computed from the track's loudness so the music sits under the voice. `level` chooses: "recommended" sets that starting level (and the mixer's ducking and fades), even on the track already placed; "keep" keeps the level of the music in place, even for another track; without it, a different track starts at the recommended level and the same track keeps its settings. The answer says which applied: given, recommended or kept. check_audio then says how loud the music sits under the voice and in the pauses. `volumeDb` sets it by hand in dB like the panel (0 = the file's own level, -40 = silent), or `volume` 0 to 1. `ducking` (default true) lowers the music while the speaker talks; `duck` picks how much: subtle (8 dB, the default), normal (12 dB) or strong (18 dB). `fadeInSec` and `fadeOutSec` (default 1 s and 3 s, 0 to 10). It replaces the music already placed, all its pieces; set_music_clip changes one piece and keeps the others. Free.

tools.name: check_audio
tools.title: Check audio
tools.description: Hear the mix, by code: the voice's level measured on spoken passages of the source, then, in dB AGAINST THE VOICE, each music track in the pauses and under the voice (after its duck), with a verdict, and the sound effects whose peak jumps over the voice or that sit less than 0.5 s apart (the ear hears one). Two readings: `preview` (the voice as recorded) and `export` (the voice after the export's chain: brought to -14 LUFS when voice is youtube, then its voiceVolumeDb, then the final limiter; music and effects stay where the mixer set them). Verdicts on music and effects use the export voice. `voice.afterChain` gives the export voice's estimated loudness (LUFS) and true peak (dBTP): `blocksExport` is true only when the voice would clip (true peak above -1 dBTP); fix that before export_video. Above -13 LUFS is a warning only (YouTube turns louder videos down to -14 LUFS). Music sits well about 15 to 25 dB under the voice. Free: no model, no credit.
